per_group_series_length.note: No panel groups; series is a single hourly sequence spanning 24 calendar months (2011-01 through 2012-12). Train rows cover days 1-19 per month (~19 hours/day x 19 days x 24 months = 10886 rows); test rows cover days 20-end per month.

target_autocorrelation.reason: Series is hourly but split within-month by day; same-month prior-day lags would be available at train time but not at inference time (test rows are later days in same month). Cross-month same-hour lags (lag=24*30=720 hours, i.e. same hour prior month) are theoretically available but require careful leakage-safe construction; treated as experimental.

sub_target_correlations.verdict: Valid sub-target: predict registered independently (train-only column, leakage as direct feature), sum with casual to form count prediction.
Valid sub-target: predict casual independently (train-only column, leakage as direct feature), sum with registered to form count prediction.

lag_features.reason: No safe same-month lags: train covers days 1-19, test covers days 20-31 within each month. Cross-month same-hour lags (720h = prior-month same-hour) would require the prior month's late-day rows which are in test; cannot be built leakage-free. Instead use within-period early-day aggregates (mean of days 1-13 per hour/weekday/month group) as the temporal signal — these are safe and high-signal.

within_period_aggregates.note: Compute within-period (early-day) group aggregates per fold; these are the leakage-safe substitute for lags in this split structure.

sub_target_modeling.rationale: registered has r=0.970 with count; casual has r=0.690. Predict each separately and sum — this is the primary accuracy lever for this dataset since sub-targets are train-only (not available at test time as direct features).
